text: Maharashtra Kharif season (June-October, monsoon-sown): common crops are rice (Konkan, Vidarbha), cotton (Vidarbha, Marathwada), soybean (Vidarbha, Marathwada), jowar, bajra, maize, tur (pigeonpeas), groundnut, and sugarcane (year-round in irrigated belts like Kolhapur, Nashik, Pune).

Maharashtra Rabi season (October-March, winter-sown, less rainfall, relies on residual moisture/irrigation): common crops are wheat, jowar (rabi jowar), gram/chickpea, sunflower, onion, and mustard in some belts. Onion is a major Rabi cash crop around Nashik.
Maharashtra summer/Zaid season (March-June, needs irrigation): watermelon, muskmelon, summer groundnut, and vegetables like tomato are common where irrigation is available.

Nashik district is well known for onion (largest onion market in India, Lasalgaon), grapes (especially for export/wine), tomato, and sugarcane in irrigated tracts. It has a moderate climate suited to horticulture crops.
Punjab Kharif season: rice (basmati and non-basmati) and cotton are dominant, along with maize and sugarcane.
Punjab Rabi season: wheat is the dominant crop, along with mustard and some gram.
Uttar Pradesh Kharif season: rice, sugarcane (grown almost year-round), maize, bajra, and pulses like arhar/tur are common.
Uttar Pradesh Rabi season: wheat is the dominant crop, along with mustard, gram, and lentil.
Gujarat Kharif season: cotton, groundnut, bajra, and sugarcane in irrigated southern belts.
Gujarat Rabi season: wheat, mustard, and gram are common, with cumin in drier regions.

Karnataka grows ragi, jowar, maize, cotton, sugarcane, coffee (Coorg/Chikmagalur hill regions), and a wide range of fruits like mango, banana, pomegranate, and grapes depending on the agro-climatic zone.
Andhra Pradesh and Telangana grow rice extensively in irrigated deltas, along with cotton, maize, groundnut, chillies, mango, and sugarcane.
Tamil Nadu grows rice, sugarcane, cotton, groundnut, and coconut extensively, along with banana and coffee in hill districts like the Nilgiris.
Madhya Pradesh is a major soybean and wheat producing state, also grows gram, cotton, and sugarcane.
Rajasthan, being arid/semi-arid, grows drought-tolerant crops: bajra, jowar, mustard, gram, and groundnut, with wheat in irrigated canal-command areas.
West Bengal is a major rice and jute producing state, also grows potato, and vegetables extensively.
